Shape.Name: Sheet.4
Shape.Text: Excite White Pixel - Theory One of the most difficult issues to troubleshoot on modern MR equipment is known as White Pixels, synonymously Spike Noise, Corduroy, Transients and Broadband Noise. Chasing down these problems can be difficult at times, even for highly experienced service engineers. Often, there will be multiple sources of the noise, which can make logical troubleshooting techniques imperative to success. In this series of articles, some of the theory of what causes them and some proven techniques in tracking down this scourge will be presented.

Shape.Name: Sheet.13
Shape.Text: The system fails epiwp. Does it fail without gradient pulsing?

Shape.Name: Procedure
Shape.Text:
If still getting spike noise after disconnecting the gradient signal fibers, the problem is not gradient related. Now need to search for spike sources that are not caused or excited by the pulsing gradients.
If the noise goes away when these fibers are disconnected, the gradients or the vibration from pulsing are the cause. Will need to further investigate to determine if it the gradients themselves or their vibration is causing the noise.

Shape.Name: Create request
Shape.Text:
Disconnect the 3 Gradient Data Fiber Optic (F/O) cables from the rear of the MGD Chassis on the STIF Board.
Repeat the epiwp test. Does it still fail?
If white pixel failures are intermittent, epiwp test must be run multiple times to determine full confidence. Example: If epiwp originally failed every 3rd pass in body mode, obtain at least 6 clean passes in body mode to be confident that problem is gradient related.

Shape.Name: Create request
Shape.Text:
Refer to the illustration and procedures in the “Sniffing for White Pixels” section (Click in this box). Connect the Head Coil with extra long BNC cables to the Quick Disconnect cable. The BNC cables between the head coil and the QD cable connector and coil should be long enough to allow the coil to be moved in and out of the bore (~6 ft.). Setup to run epiwp mode 2 on the worst case image / axis in Body Receive mode. Enable autoview and auto window/level.
Scan White pixel in the following 5 locations: 1) Isocenter 2) Front Edge of RF Tube 3) Rear Edge of RF Tube 4) Greater than 4 feet (1.3 meters) outside of the front of the bore 5) Greater than 4 feet (1.3 meters) outside of the rear of the bore

Shape.Name: Process.6
Shape.Text:
The spike noise is coming from inside or very near the magnet bore. Before tearing down, inspect once more for any metal to metal contacts. If not found, it’s time to tear things apart.
If White Pixel count is greater at isocenter, failure may be caused by Body coil or RF shield. If White Pixel count is greater at the edge of the RF tube, the RF shield, Gradient Coil or something in that general area is likely causing the White Pixel failure.
If it is an LCC magnet and the noise is originating from the gradient support bracket-LCC magnet ring interface, order and receive the following kit before tear down: Gradient Support Mounting Isolation Shim Kit 5220440 plus the tack cloth and RTV silicone described in the procedure, White Pixels Due to Particles Under BRM Bracket.
The shim kit contains two G10 shims that are positioned between the magnet ring and the gradient support bracket, isolating the two metallic parts. The White Pixels Due to Particles Under BRM Bracket procedure describes the methodology for cleaning the BRM Bracket and sealing its periphery
Continue retesting epiwp as parts are removed and ruled out.

Shape.Text:

Isolate the problem by disconnecting the receive chain progressively back toward the receiver. If the noise is still present with no input to the receiver, try running diagnostics in the System cabinet to further isolate.

Shape.Name: Create request.26
Shape.Text: Turn off all possible sources of noise. Turn modules ON one at a time until all modules are ON. If a module fails, turn it OFF and continue with the next module Turn off ROOM LIGHTS Power off COLD HEAD at the compressor EMERGENCY RUNDOWN UNIT OR MAGNET RUNDOWN UNIT – power off at its breaker which is typically in the customer panel. It may be easier to remove the fuses. CAUTION: It is prudent to disconnect the ERU / MRU from the magnet before working on or powering off the ERU / MRU!!! Disconnect the OXYGEN MONITOR at the Penetration Panel (this will trigger the oxygen alarm) or power it off at its breaker in the customer panel Disconnect the cable to the ENCODER at the magnet IF If you have a MAGNET GROUND, make sure that it has a good connection at the magnet and at the room shield. Turn off CHILLER Check for burned out room lights and remove them. Turn off HELIUM MONITOR Turn off RF DOOR SWITCH Turn off BLOWER Turn off HEAT EXCHANGER Turn off EXHAUST FANS Use your imagination to troubleshoot items that may be unique to the room. Examples include power injectors, music systems, add-on patient monitoring devices, hospital alarm systems, back-lit artwork, etc.

HLURL:Hyperlink.HLURL:AbsoluteURL: L:\MR Troubleshooting Flowcharts\5155500 Signa HDx 14.0\Cord\5182010 revC.vsd#Page-1

Shape.Name: Sheet.1
Shape.Text:
The High Pass Body coil’s Dynamic Disable and Direct Drive Disable biases are the same on 1.5T CRM, BRM, and TRMs as well as on all 1.0T and 0.5T Body coils. Below is the biasing scheme for these coils: Body mode: Diodes are reverse biased with a high voltage (1000 or 500v). Head mode: Diodes are forward biased with a relatively low voltage but regulated current (current sink mode)
This means that when bias cables are disconnected during troubleshooting the devices will revert to “Body mode”. The unbiased diodes act like opens, just like reverse biased diodes. Since we are troubleshooting broadband spike noise, the receive coils will still act as antennae adequate for receiving the spikes in this mode. The body coil will remain connected to the normal receive path through the Body Hybrid if the Direct Drive Disable bias cable is disconnected.
T/R biasing is: Reverse bias = receive, Forward bias = transmit. Disconnecting T/R Bias puts the diodes in receive mode
Note: To prevent damage to the diodes, never transmit into any RF coil when any diode circuits are unbiased.

HLURL:Hyperlink.HLURL:AbsoluteURL: L:\MR Troubleshooting Flowcharts\5155500 Signa HDx 14.0\Cord\5182010 revC.vsd#appendix-2
L:\MR Troubleshooting Flowcharts\5155500 Signa HDx 14.0\Cord\5182010 revC.vsd#appendix-1

Shape.Name: Sheet.2
Shape.Text:
The G3 Body coil’s Dynamic Disable and Direct Drive Disable biases are of reversed polarity as compared to 3T94, and 1.5T CRM, BRM, and TRMs. Below is the biasing scheme for the G3 coils:
Body mode: Diodes are forward biased with a relatively low voltage but regulated current (current sink mode) Head mode: Diodes are reverse biased with a high voltage (500v).
This means that when bias cables are disconnected during troubleshooting the devices will revert to “Head mode”. The unbiased diodes act like opens, just like reverse biased diodes. Since we are troubleshooting broadband spike noise, the body coil will still act as an antenna for receiving the spikes in this mode. However, the coil will be disconnected from the normal receive path through the Body Hybrid if the Direct Drive Disable bias cable is disconnected.
T/R biasing is still the same (ie. Reverse bias = receive, Forward bias = transmit)
Note: To prevent damage to the diodes, never transmit into any RF coil when any diode circuits are unbiased.
